recipes.name: Hoisin Sauce
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, sweet and savory, with prune, mashed black beans and five-spice warmth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fermented black beans bring depth of flavor; the sauce is sweet and salty, so a little goes far.

components.note: 5 tbsp fermented black beans, mashed to the paste the source uses

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Mash the fermented black beans to a paste.
Put everything in a blender and blend until smooth.
Keep in a jar in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: High, from the soy sauce and fermented black beans.
From the brown sugar and prunes.

recipes.curationNote: Cuisine (NZ), Homemade Hoisin Sauce for every amount and step; makes 1 cup, scaled to our 20 tbsp (x1.25): 4 tbsp fermented black bean paste, 8 prunes finely chopped, 4 tbsp soy sauce, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 2 tbsp rice wine vinegar, 1/2 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp Chinese five spice; all blended smooth, no cooking.

recipes.name: Pao Jiao (Sichuan Pickled Chilies)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sour, salty and hot, with a rounded fermented depth.
recipes.healthBenefit: A lacto-fermented pickle; chilies keep much of their vitamin C, and the brine is salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: whole, stems on, washed and dried

ingredients.prepNote: in place of Sichuan peppercorns, which the database does not hold

ingredients.baseName: Alcoholic beverage, spirit, ~40% v/v, all (Brandy, Gin, Rum, Vodka and Whisky)

instructions: Dissolve the salt and rock sugar in the cooled boiled water in a clean pickling jar. Add the ginger, Sichuan pepper and spirit.
Push the chillies under the brine, weight them down and close the jar, using a water-seal lid if you have one.
Leave at cool room temperature for 2 to 3 weeks, until sour. Keep the brine going with fresh vegetables. One serving is 20 g of chillies.

nutritionHighlights.note: Chilies keep much of their vitamin C in the brine.
Salty: count it if you watch sodium.

citations.source: The Mala Market, Sichuan's naturally fermented pickles

recipes.curationNote: The Mala Market, Sichuan's naturally fermented pickles (pao cai brine) for every amount and step; its brine (per cup of water 14 to 16 g salt, 4 g rock sugar, 4 g baijiu, Sichuan pepper optional) is used for fresh chillies and ginger too; scaled to our 1 L.

recipes.name: Suan Dou Jiao (Pickled Long Beans)
recipes.healthBenefit: A lacto-fermented pickle that brings fiber; the brine is salty.

ingredients.baseName: Alcoholic beverage, spirit, ~40% v/v, all (Brandy, Gin, Rum, Vodka and Whisky)

instructions: Dissolve the salt and rock sugar in the cooled boiled water in a clean jar and add the ginger, chillies and spirit.
Coil the beans into the jar under the brine, weight them down and close.
Leave at cool room temperature for 5 to 7 days, until sour and olive green. One serving is 20 g of beans.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beans.
Salty: count it if you watch sodium.

citations.source: The Mala Market, Sichuan's naturally fermented pickles

recipes.curationNote: The Mala Market, Sichuan's naturally fermented pickles (pao cai brine) for every amount and step; per cup of water 14 to 16 g salt, 4 g rock sugar, 4 g baijiu; long beans, ginger and chillies are among its listed vegetables; scaled to our 1 L.

recipes.name: Chen Pi (Dried Citrus Peel)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bittersweet, fragrant and citrusy, deepening as it ages.
recipes.healthBenefit: Used a piece at a time for flavor; it adds almost nothing but aroma.

ingredients.cutPrep: peel of about 8 oranges, white pith scraped thin
ingredients.prepNote: mandarin peel is traditional; the database has orange peel

instructions: Scrape away most of the white pith and cut the peel into pieces.
Dry in the sun or a 50 C (120 F) oven until brittle, a few days in the sun or about 6 hours in the oven.
Keep in a closed jar; it improves with age. Soak a piece in warm water for 20 minutes before using.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the peel.

recipes.name: Xian Ya Dan (Salted Duck Eggs)
recipes.flavorProfile: Very salty whites and rich, sandy, orange yolks.
recipes.healthBenefit: Duck eggs are rich in protein, vitamin B12 and selenium; salting makes them very high in sodium.
instructions: Boil the water with the salt until dissolved and cool completely, then stir in the spirit.
Put the eggs in a clean jar, pour the brine over, weight them under and close.
Leave in a cool, dry place for 30 to 60 days, testing one egg at 30 days. Steam or boil before eating.

nutritionHighlights.note: Duck eggs are rich in B12.
Very high; one egg carries most of a day's worth.

citations.source: The Woks of Life, Salted Duck Eggs

recipes.curationNote: The Woks of Life, Salted Duck Eggs for every amount and step; 12 duck eggs, 1 quart water, 1/4 cup (70 g) sea salt, 1/2 cup baijiu, 30 to 60 days; star anise, cinnamon and Sichuan pepper are optional and left out.

recipes.name: Xian Dan Huang (Salted Egg Yolks)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, sandy and savory, the center of zongzi and mooncakes.
recipes.healthBenefit: Egg yolk brings vitamins A, D and B12 and choline; salting makes it high in sodium.

ingredients.cutPrep: from 12 eggs brined whole, whites set aside for another dish
ingredients.prepNote: duck yolks are traditional; the database has chicken yolk

instructions: Brine 12 whole eggs in the water, salt and spirit as for salted duck eggs, 30 to 60 days.
Crack them, keep the whites for another dish and lift out the firm yolks.
Rinse each yolk and bake at 150 C (300 F) for 8 minutes before using.

nutritionHighlights.note: Egg yolk is one of the richest sources of choline.
High.

recipes.name: Dou Sha (Sweet Red Bean Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, earthy and smooth, with the taste of adzuki beans.
recipes.healthBenefit: Adzuki beans bring fiber, folate and plant protein, alongside the sugar.
instructions: Cover the soaked beans well with water and simmer about 1 1/2 hours, until they crush easily, topping up the water if needed.
Drain the beans and blend them to a paste, skins and all.
Cook the paste in a nonstick pan with the sugar and salt, adding the oil a spoonful at a time and stirring constantly, until it is thick and pulls away from the pan, about 30 minutes.
Cool and keep in the fridge a week or freeze.

nutritionHighlights.note: About 2 g per tablespoon.
About 6 g per tablespoon.

recipes.name: Lap Cheong (Chinese Sausage)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, salty and fragrant, firm from drying, with diced fat that melts when cooked.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and B vitamins; the sausage is sweet and fatty, so it seasons a dish.

ingredients.cutPrep: cut in 5 mm dice, blanched and drained

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Alcoholic beverage, spirit, ~40% v/v, all (Brandy, Gin, Rum, Vodka and Whisky)
ingredients.prepNote: in place of rose wine (mei kuei lu chiew), which the database does not hold

ingredients.baseName: Pork, offal and by-products, small intestine
ingredients.prepNote: about 2 m for 1 kg of filling

instructions: Mix the diced meat and fat with the sugar, salt, soy, spirit, black pepper and red yeast rice powder and leave 1 hour.
Stuff into the casing, prick out any air and tie into 20 links of about 15 cm.

Hang in a cool, dry, airy place (or at 50 C, 122 F, in a low oven with the door ajar for the first day) for 7 to 10 days, until firm and about a third lighter. They keep a month in the fridge. Steam or slice into the dish.

nutritionHighlights.note: About 4.5 g per sausage.
Close to 600 mg per sausage, from the salt and soy sauce.

recipes.healthBenefit: Pork belly brings B vitamins; it is mostly fat, so a little seasons a pot of rice.

ingredients.cutPrep: skin on, in strips 4 cm wide

recipes.name: Wu Xiang Dougan (Spiced Dried Tofu)
recipes.flavorProfile: Firm, chewy and savoury, braised in soy with star anise, cinnamon, cloves and bay.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pressing concentrates the protein of tofu.

ingredients.baseName: Tofu, firm, prepared with calcium sulfate and magnesium chloride (nigari)
ingredients.cutPrep: pressed under a weight for 4 hours
ingredients.prepNote: about a third of the weight is pressed out as water

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
ingredients.prepNote: about 11 ml; in place of dark soy sauce, which the database does not hold
one small piece of cinnamon or cassia bark

instructions: Press the tofu between boards under a heavy weight for 4 hours, until firm and dense.
Simmer the water, light and dark soy sauce, sugar, salt, star anise, cloves, bay leaves, cinnamon and white peppercorns for 10 minutes.
Add the pressed tofu and simmer gently 30 minutes, then leave it in the liquid overnight.
Lift out and dry on a rack, or in a low oven, until the surface is firm. It makes about 700 g.

recipes.name: Bai Fu Ru (White Fermented Bean Curd)
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy, salty and pungent, a little like strong cheese.
recipes.healthBenefit: Used a cube at a time as a seasoning; it is salty.

ingredients.baseName: Tofu, firm, prepared with calcium sulfate and magnesium chloride (nigari)
ingredients.cutPrep: pressed and cut in 2.5 cm cubes

ingredients.prepNote: for the simmering water, which is poured away
dissolved in the brine the cubes are kept and served in
optional; about 2 dried chillies, for half the cubes
optional; in place of Sichuan pepper, which the database does not hold

instructions: Simmer the tofu 5 minutes in water with the 13 g salt, drain, then press it between towels under a heavy weight until as dry as possible.
Cut into 2.5 cm cubes, set them apart on paper towel, cover loosely and keep in a warm, dark place about 3 days, until spotted with mould. Throw away any cube that turns slimy, pink or black.
Boil the brine water with the 39 g salt, the sugar, Sichuan pepper and star anise for 2 minutes, cool completely, stir in the Shaoxing wine and strain out the spices.
Pack the cubes into sterilised jars, coating some in the chopped chilli if you like, and pour in brine to cover. Close and keep in a warm, dark place at least 3 months before using.

nutritionHighlights.note: About 380 mg sodium per cube.
About 2 g protein per cube.

recipes.name: Nam Yu (Red Fermented Bean Curd)
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty, winey and savoury, deep red.
recipes.healthBenefit: Used a cube at a time as a seasoning; it is salty.

ingredients.baseName: Tofu, firm, prepared with calcium sulfate and magnesium chloride (nigari)

ingredients.prepNote: a little sprinkled on the squares, the rest stirred into the sauce

ingredients.name: red yeast rice powder
ingredients.prepNote: hong qu, gives the red colour

ingredients.name: dried rose buds, ground
ingredients.prepNote: grind the dried buds to a powder

instructions: Cut the tofu into 2.5 cm squares, lay them on a baking sheet and sprinkle with a little of the salt.
Dry them in the oven at 65 C (150 F) for 1 hour, turning them over halfway.
Stir the rest of the salt, the brown sugar, red yeast rice powder, ground rose buds and Shaoxing wine together.
Put the tofu in a clean jar that seals, pour the red mixture over and close it.
Keep it somewhere dark at about 20 C (68 F) for 3 to 6 months; the longer it sits, the softer and stronger it gets. Use a little at a time with rice, congee, stir-fries or braises.

nutritionHighlights.note: About 380 mg sodium per cube.

recipes.name: Douchi (Fermented Black Soybeans)
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty, savoury and deeply fermented, with soft beans.
recipes.healthBenefit: A seasoning used by the spoonful; it is very salty.

ingredients.prepNote: black soybeans are traditional; no food database here lists them dry, so yellow soybeans stand in
non-iodised; 90 g for the beans, 18 g for the top

instructions: Soak the beans overnight in plenty of water.
Drain them, cover with fresh water and simmer for about 1 1/2 hours, until soft.
Drain, keeping 120 ml (1/2 cup) of the cooking water, and let the beans and the water cool for 1 to 2 hours.
Toss the beans with 90 g (5 tbsp) of the salt.
Put half the beans in a clean 1 quart (1 litre) jar, spoon the miso into the middle, and cover it with the rest of the beans.
Scatter the last 18 g (1 tbsp) of salt on top, set a weight on the beans and pour in the saved water, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) of space.
Close the jar with a lid that lets gas escape and keep it in the dark for at least 2 months, up to 6. Once opened, keep it in the fridge.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt; very salty, so a little goes a long way.
From the soybeans.

citations.source: Fermenting for Foodies, Fermented Black Beans Simplified (Douchi)
